_about: Limits for the pixel style, for tools/look.mjs --check: node tools/look.mjs --shots hills,wood,coast,alpine,valley,river,desert,city,cavern,inferno,abyss,heaven,space,upside,meadow --styles real,pixel --check tools/look/pixel.json (npm run check:pixel runs it after tools/pixel_check.mjs). The same kind of rule as in targets.json. A frame of the pixel style is a grid of cells in the 24 colours of a world's palette, so what is held is what such a frame is: cells of one colour, no more colours than a palette has, nothing burnt out, a line round the car, a clean far land, and a frame that draws no more than the real style's and takes clearly less time.

rules.why: a frame has the colours of one palette and no others, a cell counting for one (22 to 24 measured)
every pixel is the colour of its cell: a cell is a block of whole pixels of one colour (1 measured)
nothing is burnt white: the lightest colour of a palette is a warm off-white (0 measured)

the car has a line of the darkest grey round it, a cell wide: of the pixels on its edge the share with a dark one (L under 0.38) within 2 px (0.894 measured; the line is a cell, 3 px on this canvas, beyond the car's cells, and the car's edge in the map lies up to 2 px inside the last of them)
the car has a line round it (0.900 measured)
the car has a line round it (0.900 measured)
the car has a line round it (0.968 measured)
the car has a line round it (0.977 measured)
the car has a line round it (0.933 measured)

the car has a line round it; the car is turned in the bend and its edge runs across the cells at a slant, so fewer of its edge pixels have the line within 2 px (0.813 measured; the line is there all the way round)
the far land (300 to 1500 m) is flat faces in a few colours, no fine texture (0.011 measured)
the far land does not change from one frame to the next the car's sixtieth of a second on (0.0027 measured)
no more draw calls than the real style (2 to 12 fewer: no glow, no style pass)
no more triangles than the real style by more than the grass's outer ring and the map of the land it is laid from (0.97 to 1.10 measured)

software rendering: the scene is drawn at 0.45 of the canvas's pixels here (a ninth at 1080p) but with the real style's geometry, so a frame takes 0.6 to 0.7 of the real one's (the mean over the shots; a frame's time moves several per cent a run)
